spacing.note: Values are vw-locked multiples of 1.6667px at a 1440px viewport (root ≈ 1.157vw).

shadows: hero globe only: 4-layer orange inset glow (rgb 255,85,0) and 2-layer blue inset glow (rgb 1,47,255)

taste.name: One vehicle narrates every scene
taste.trigger: When a freight company had to explain several services (road, air, ocean) on one long page
taste.decision: Chose a single cut-out product object that re-enters each scene from a new camera angle (side-on truck, top-down on a road, underside of a plane) over per-service illustrations, icons or photo cards
taste.reason: Because a visitor follows an object more readily than a list: the same truck changing viewpoint turns scrolling into travelling, so the services feel like legs of one trip
evidence: top-down truck on a #111111 road strip at 50% scroll
plane seen from below at 75% scroll

taste.name: Colour is spent once, in the first viewport
taste.trigger: When choosing where the brand's energy should show
taste.decision: Chose to confine chromatic colour to the hero globe's inset glows (#FF5500, #012FFF, one shadow declaration each) and run the remaining 28 000px in #FFFFFF / #111111 / #000000, over a brand accent repeated on buttons, links and icons
taste.reason: Because a single burst of colour at the door reads as an event; after it, the neutral field lets the vehicles' own metal and paint be the only things with presence
evidence: 2 chromatic shadows total, both on the hero
buttons are white or #111 pills, never coloured

taste.name: Telemetry voice for small print
taste.trigger: When setting labels, nav and status text that sit around huge headlines
taste.decision: Chose a monospaced companion (BT Steinhart Mono, 92 nodes at 7.5–10px) for HUD-like readouts such as '00 KM/H' over setting small UI text in the body sans
taste.reason: Because numbers and labels in a mono cut read as instruments, which makes the page feel measured and in motion rather than decorated
evidence: '00 KM/H' readout top-left of each vehicle scene

taste.name: Ghosted first word instead of an eyebrow
taste.trigger: When a section headline needed a lead-in
taste.decision: Chose to set the first word of the headline at rgba(17,17,17,0.16) and the rest at #111111 ('RELIABILITY / AT EVERY MILESTONE') over a small coloured eyebrow label or an accent-coloured keyword
taste.reason: Because the reader still reads one continuous statement, but the eye lands on the second half first, so emphasis comes from value contrast rather than an extra element
